title: Roz Brewer Talks College Aid, Walgreens During Covid and Retail
summary: Spelman College Chair Emerita Rosalind "Roz" Brewer, former CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance, says that she "never looked back to the lab" after moving from working as an organic chemist at Kimberly-Clarke to moving to the corporate side of the business. Speaking to Romaine Bostick at Bloomberg New Voices in Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts, Brewer says that the timing of her joining Walgreens during the Covid-19 pandemic gave her the best chance to make changes, as times of crisis often provide the best opportunities to do so. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chip Rout Clouds Asia Open as Bond Jitters Linger: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks in Asia were set to fall Wednesday after a selloff in US technology shares, as elevated bond yields, rising oil prices and renewed Middle East tensions prompted investors to pare risk.

title: Gluten-Free Brand Breaks Out in Saturated Market
summary: Feel Good Foods has been selling gluten-free frozen foods since 2012, eventually starting to outsell legacy frozen food brands like PF Chang's and TGI Fridays. CEO Vanessa Phillips founded the brand after being diagnosed with celiac disease and college, and refusing to give up her favorite foods. She says the brand doesn't just serve gluten-free consumers, saying most customers buy the product because it "works for them and their lifestyle." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: KKR Real Estate Lender’s Woes Attract Investment Firm Mavik
summary: An investment firm that specializes in commercial real estate distress is betting that a lender managed by KKR & Co. is likely to sell its loan portfolio at or around book value.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
summary: Oil rose for a fourth day, with no sign of progress toward a resolution of the US-Iran war after almost six months of conflict.

title: Roz Brewer Says US Retail Needs Global Partners
summary: Spelman College Chair Emerita Rosalind "Roz" Brewer, former CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance, discusses the state of the US consumer in the current economy with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg New Voices event in Martha’s Vineyard. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Revolution's Hall On Investing in the Defense Sector
summary: David Hall, managing partner at Revolution, talks about investing in the defense sector and backing Hermeus, a company looking to build a hyper-sonic military jet. He speaks with Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg New Voices event in Martha's Vineyard. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Falls as Traders Weigh US Inflation
summary: Gold valuation platform Unvault estimates that American households are sitting on $750 Billion worth of gold, largely in the form of unworn jewelry. The company says consumers consistently underestimate their jewelry's spot value by 3x or more because pieces purchased prior to 2010 have more than tripled in value. CEO Nidhi Singhvi joins Businessweek Daily to discuss how her business is being boosting by higher gold prices in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fletcher Building Waiting on Meaningful Recovery in NZ Demand
summary: New Zealand’s largest construction materials company Fletcher Building Ltd. doesn’t expect a meaningful recovery in its markets until 2027, adding to signs of muted economic growth over the second half of this year.

title: Ex-Tricolor Executives Face SEC Lawsuit After Firm Collapse
summary: Tricolor Holdings founder Daniel Chu, who already faces federal criminal charges, and two other former executives were sued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission for allegedly defrauding investors before the used car seller and subprime lender imploded.

title: Uruguay Holds Interest Rates Steady With Inflation Below Target
summary: Uruguay’s central bank held interest rates steady for a fourth consecutive policy meeting with inflation below its target.

title: Walter Probe Weighs on Carvana as Traders Suspect Share Sale
summary: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. dropped Tuesday, hurt by concerns that one of the company’s largest investors — billionaire Mark Walter — may sell down his stake as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.

title: EM Rally Stalls Amid Surge in Treasury Yields, Mideast Tensions
summary: The recent rally in emerging-market assets stalled on Tuesday as a surge in long-term US Treasury yields and renewed tensions in the Middle East drained demand for risk, snapping a four-day winning streak in stocks and pushing borrowing costs higher.

title: Power Broker Frances Katzen on Pending Home Sales Slide
summary: Frances Katzen, founder of The Katzen Team and a top broker at Douglas Elliman in New York City, discussed the current dynamics of the housing market, highlighting a pronounced K-shaped trend. While overall housing activity has slowed, the high-end segment in Manhattan is experiencing significant growth, with contract signings up 39% year-over-year in October and properties priced between $3 million and $5 million up 27%. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bond Traders Bite at Microsoft-Tied Data Center Junk-Like Yields
summary: Blackstone Inc.-backed QTS Realty Trust Inc. offered junk-like yields on a $3.9 billion high-grade bond to fund the construction of a Microsoft Corp.-linked data center in Georgia. It looks to have worked as the deal racked up demand of about six times that amount.

title: Energy Stocks Hit Record as Oil Rises on Fading Deal Hopes
summary: Energy stocks closed at the first record since March as investors see diminishing prospects for a near-term ceasefire in the Iran war that could ease the standoff in the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

title: Gold Falls as Traders Weigh US Inflation, Rates Amid Bond Rout
summary: Gold declined as traders evaluated the outlook for US inflation and interest rates amid a global government bond rout.

title: Bond Traders Are Hedging Risk Fed Pivots to Rate Cuts in 2027
summary: Bond traders are changing gears again. After a raft of data helped all but price out interest rate hikes for the rest of the year, wagers in the options market are looking to hedge the risk that the Federal Reserve pivots to cutting rates in 2027.

title: Ripple’s Brokerage Arm Taps Private Placement Bond Market
summary: The prime-brokerage arm of digital-asset company Ripple has raised $275 million through the private placement bond market.

title: Stocks Fall As Global Bond Yields Stay Elevated | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Scarlet, Fu, Isabelle Lee, Carol Massar and Joe Deaux. (Source: Bloomberg)
